sources.title: BIT 216 Data Structures and Algorithms Course Outline

questions.prompt: Which principle describes the order in which items leave a stack?
questions.explanation: A stack uses last-in-first-out (LIFO): the most recently pushed item is popped first.

questions.prompt: Which sequence is followed when removing elements from a standard queue?
What condition is necessary for the binary search procedure described in the lecture notes?
options: The list uses a linked list
The first key equals the target
questions.explanation: Binary search compares the target with the middle item and discards one half, which assumes a sorted sequence.

questions.prompt: What is the asymptotic time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n items?
questions.explanation: Each step halves the remaining search range, giving logarithmic complexity.

questions.prompt: A sequential search for an absent key in an array of n records makes at most how many key comparisons, in the worst case?
questions.explanation: When the target is absent, sequential search examines all n records.

questions.prompt: What is selected at each pass of ascending selection sort as taught in the notes?
options: The smallest element of the unsorted portion
The middle element as a pivot
questions.explanation: Selection sort chooses the smallest remaining element and moves it into its sorted position.

questions.prompt: Selection sort performs approximately how many comparisons as the array size n grows?
questions.explanation: The comparison count is (n−1)+(n−2)+...+1 = n(n−1)/2, which is O(n²).

questions.prompt: Which worst-case complexity is given for mergesort in the sorting lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture describes mergesort's worst-case running time as O(n log n).

questions.prompt: In preorder traversal of a binary tree, what is visited first?
questions.explanation: Preorder is root, left subtree, right subtree.

questions.section: Heap Sort Approach / Implementation using arrays
questions.prompt: In a zero-indexed array representation of a binary heap, what are the child indices of the item at index i?
questions.explanation: For a zero-based binary heap, children of index i are at 2i+1 and 2i+2 when those positions exist.

questions.prompt: Describe the binary search algorithm for finding a key in a sorted array. Include the search bounds, middle-element comparison, and stopping condition. (5 marks)
questions.explanation: An acceptable solution sets low and high bounds, chooses a middle index, compares the target with the middle value, retains the appropriate half, and terminates when found or when the range is empty.

rubric.description: States that binary search operates on a sorted array and initializes low/high bounds.
Calculates or identifies the middle element of the current search interval.
Compares the target with the middle element, returning when equal.
Updates low or high to discard the irrelevant half.
Repeats while low <= high and correctly describes the not-found outcome.

questions.prompt: Differentiate bubble sort and selection sort, explaining how each proceeds through an unsorted array and describing their general comparison complexity. (5 marks)
questions.explanation: Bubble sort repeatedly swaps out-of-order neighbors, whereas selection sort chooses the smallest element in the remaining unsorted portion. Both standard versions have quadratic comparison complexity.

rubric.description: Describes bubble sort's repeated adjacent comparisons.
Explains that bubble sort swaps out-of-order neighbors.
Describes selecting the minimum element from the unsorted portion in selection sort.
Explains moving that element to its sorted position.
Identifies O(n²) general comparison complexity for both algorithms.
